answer_as_filed:
Wyandot Memorial Hospital participates in the 340B Drug Pricing Program as a critical access hospital to support its mission of providing accessible, high-quality care to all patients, regardless of ability to pay. Savings generated through the program are reinvested into patient care, service line support, workforce development, and community health initiatives that directly benefit the population served.
While the organization does not maintain a fully itemized accounting of each dollar of 340B program profit by individual expenditure, it monitors program performance through aggregate financial reporting, including total acquisition costs, reimbursement, and estimated net program savings. These funds are incorporated into the hospital’s operating budget and strategically allocated to sustain and expand essential services.
Although specific dollar amounts are not allocated at the individual program level, the organization uses its budgeting, financial reporting, and leadership oversight processes to ensure that 340B savings are reinvested into patient care, access-related services, community health initiatives, workforce support, and other programs that benefit the patients and communities served.
340B program savings directly and indirectly support a variety of programs, services, and initiatives, including but not limited to:
•	Lab Screening Program – Provides accessible and discounted health screenings through community health fairs and walk-in services, supporting early detection, prevention, and population health management through the hospital’s voucher system. Support from 340B savings helps reduce financial barriers for individuals who may otherwise delay or avoid routine laboratory testing due to cost. These screenings allow patients and community members to identify potential health concerns earlier, connect with appropriate follow-up care, and take proactive steps to manage chronic conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and other preventable or treatable health risks.
•	Patient Navigator Program – Offers individualized care coordination and assistance securing resources for medications, follow-up services, specialty care, transportation needs, financial assistance, and other support services that may impact a patient’s ability to access care. Support from 340B savings helps sustain this role by allowing the hospital to connect patients with available programs, reduce barriers related to cost or logistics, and provide guidance throughout the care process. This support is especially important for patients managing chronic conditions, complex treatment plans, or limited resources, as it helps improve continuity of care, medication adherence, and timely access to needed services.
•	Community Health Education – Supports a wide range of school-based and community-based education efforts designed to improve health literacy, promote prevention, and connect individuals with resources before health concerns become more serious. These efforts include community health fairs, disease-specific education such as diabetic and cardiac education, stroke education, CPR training, Babysitter Clinic, career day activities, support groups, and other outreach events that address identified community needs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital offer these programs in accessible formats, often at low or no cost to participants, while extending education beyond the hospital walls and into the communities it serves. These initiatives strengthen prevention efforts, encourage early intervention, support chronic disease management, and help individuals and families make informed decisions about their health and wellness.
•	Charity Care Program – Ensures access to medically necessary healthcare services for low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and underserved patients who may not qualify for other assistance programs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital continue providing care regardless of a patient’s ability to pay, reduces financial barriers that may prevent individuals from seeking timely treatment, and supports follow-up care, diagnostic services, medication access, and other resources needed to promote better health outcomes within the community.
•	Student Education and Workforce Development – Supports clinical training, student placement, mentorship, and education programs for pharmacy, nursing, and allied health students, including partnerships with regional colleges and international programs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital invest in the development of future healthcare professionals by providing hands-on learning opportunities in a rural hospital setting. These experiences expose students to critical access hospital operations, interdisciplinary care, medication management, patient-centered service delivery, and the unique healthcare needs of rural communities. 
•	Population Health and Public Health Initiatives – Includes participation in community health needs assessments, opioid reduction efforts, public health campaigns, and prevention-based programs designed to improve overall community wellness. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital identify and respond to priority health needs within the community, particularly for rural, underserved, and at-risk populations. These efforts include initiatives focused on chronic disease prevention, behavioral health awareness, substance use prevention and recovery support, immunization and screening education, injury prevention, healthy lifestyle promotion, and coordination with local public health and community partners. In addition to these programmatic investments, 340B savings support staffing resources, care delivery infrastructure, and operational stability, ensuring continued access to essential healthcare services in a rural setting.
As a critical access hospital serving a rural population, these reinvestments are essential to maintaining access to care, addressing health disparities, and supporting services that would otherwise be financially unsustainable. The organization remains committed to using 340B program benefits in a manner that aligns with both federal program intent and the healthcare needs of the community.
Wyandot Memorial Hospital maintains appropriate oversight and compliance processes to ensure adherence to 340B program requirements and responsible stewardship of program resources, with a continued focus on improving patient access, affordability, and quality of care.
